claim: Even if the SFT/RL train-time intervention only partially breaks confidence collapse, the RAW internal sampling-confidence signal (measured pre-intervention at ECE 0.059, AUROC 0.987 on HumanEval) can be wrapped in a risk-controlled selective-generation scheme (CIC-style conformal abstention) targeting ~70-90% coverage at <=2-5% error at alpha=0.10, providing a defensible secondary/fallback headline distinct from the verbal-discrimination result.
stance_target: pre-registered fallback plan if DPRC's trained per-requirement expressed confidence underperforms
scope_conditions: HumanEval + MBPP calibration pool, single-GPU LoRA setup
quoted_support: Pre-registered fallback: CIC-style risk-controlled selective generation wrapped on the RAW internal sampling-confidence signal (never the SFT-collapsed verbal output) targets ~70-90% coverage at <=2-5% error at alpha=0.10

claim: The base paper's SFT intervention (274 examples, LoRA r=16) reduced verbal ECE by 64% but collapsed discrimination entirely -- the SFT model assigned mean confidence 0.900 to both easy and hard HumanEval problems, i.e. the expressed distribution degenerated to a single default bin.
stance_target: naive SFT-only approaches to training expressed confidence in code LLMs
scope_conditions: HumanEval (164 problems), Qwen2.5-Coder-family model, LoRA r=16, 274 SFT examples
quoted_support: the SFT intervention (274 examples, LoRA r=16) reduces verbal ECE by 64% but collapses discrimination -- the SFT model assigns mean confidence 0.900 to both easy and hard problems, i.e., the expressed distribution degenerates to a single default bin.
